entries.input: Alice and Bob play with a string of $n$ digits, each of which is $0$, $1$ or $2$; every digit starts at $0$. A move adds $1$ to one digit or subtracts $1$ from one digit, and is legal only if the resulting string has not occurred before in the game. A player with no legal move loses. Alice moves first. Prove that for every $n \geq 1$ it is Bob who has a winning strategy.
entries.name: Putnam2025A3
entries.conclusion: ∃ bob : List (Fin n → ℕ) → (Fin n → ℕ), (∀ p : List (Fin n → ℕ), p.head? = some (fun _ => 0) → p.Nodup → (∀ v ∈ p, ∀ i, v i ≤ 2) → List.IsChain (fun a b => ∃ i, (∀ j, j ≠ i → a j = b j) ∧ (b i = a i + 1 ∨ a i = b i + 1)) p → (∀ k, 0 < k → 2 * k < p.length → p[2 * k]? = some (bob (p.take (2 * k)))) → Even p.length → (∃ w, (∀ i, w i ≤ 2) ∧ w ∉ p ∧ ∀ a ∈ p.getLast?, (fun a b => ∃ i, (∀ j, j ≠ i → a j = b j) ∧ (b i = a i + 1 ∨ a i = b i + 1)) a w) → ((∀ i, bob p i ≤ 2) ∧ bob p ∉ p ∧ ∀ a ∈ p.getLast?, (fun a b => ∃ i, (∀ j, j ≠ i → a j = b j) ∧ (b i = a i + 1 ∨ a i = b i + 1)) a (bob p))) ∧ (∀ p : List (Fin n → ℕ), p.head? = some (fun _ => 0) → p.Nodup → (∀ v ∈ p, ∀ i, v i ≤ 2) → List.IsChain (fun a b => ∃ i, (∀ j, j ≠ i → a j = b j) ∧ (b i = a i + 1 ∨ a i = b i + 1)) p → (∀ k, 0 < k → 2 * k < p.length → p[2 * k]? = some (bob (p.take (2 * k)))) → (∀ w, (∀ i, w i ≤ 2) → w ∉ p → ∀ a ∈ p.getLast?, ¬ (fun a b => ∃ i, (∀ j, j ≠ i → a j = b j) ∧ (b i = a i + 1 ∨ a i = b i + 1)) a w) → Odd p.length)
